- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect bearish pressure.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 1–3% upward bias to the next 3–5 day horizon.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and forecast deviates >3% from true outcome, apply mean reversion: align forecast to 20-day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >5% over 5 days), reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overestimating momentum.
